description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs lines 877-885: check_inputs detects "duplicate certificates" by comparing SubjectPublicKeyInfo equality. The intent (line 879 comment) is to detect a cert appearing twice in the chain. However, the comparison is value-based on the SPKI fields, not identity-based on the certificate itself. Two legitimately different certificates that happen to share the same public key (e.g., a cross-signed cert from two different CAs, both carrying the same subject public key) will trigger DuplicateCertificate even though neither cert is a duplicate.

More critically for correctness: the comment at line 185-188 in the DuplicateCertificate error doc says "two distinct certificates that share the same public key... indicates a likely error in chain construction." This framing is incorrect. In a cross-certification topology, it is entirely valid for two different CA certificates to share a key (one CA, two different issuers). Rejecting such chains is a correctness bug.

Additionally, the check fires before chain_walk, so a valid cross-signed chain would be rejected with DuplicateCertificate before signature verification even attempts it, giving no opportunity for the signature path to succeed.

The DFS path builder cycle detection (pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs line 238) also uses SPKI identity for cycle detection — this is correct there because within the same chain the same signing key appearing twice is a cycle. But in validate_path, the same assumption means a legitimately cross-signed chain is rejected.

Suggested fix: compare full certificate identity (e.g., require both SPKI AND issuer+serial match) rather than SPKI alone. Or limit the check to exact certificate equality (same DER bytes), not SPKI value equality.
title: P0: DuplicateCertificate check uses SPKI equality — false-positive on key reuse across chain
